title: What have you stopped asking for?

notes.point: What have you stopped asking for?
notes.story: Ask people to recall a problem they stopped trying to solve. Introduce Alan, then connect the question to changing development economics.
Explain how familiar technologies and available skills shaped product choices. These were rational constraints, but not always the ideal starting point.

title: What should we build?
body:
Think beyond your constraints.
Build with AI.
Deliver with discipline.

notes.story: AI expands realistic options. Product and engineering judgment choose among them. AI can accelerate an ordinary application without being a feature of it.

title: Build the right tool
body: A better authoring workflow can improve everything downstream

notes.story: Compare specialized authoring with familiar tools plus import. Discuss potential organizational benefits without invented metrics. Sometimes recognizing the wrong tool is the valuable work.

title: Open it and log
body:
No registration.
No setup ritual.
Start logging.

notes.story: Describe the personal gym problem and desired experience. Explain the mobile-friendly PWA and local anonymous device-specific data. AI accelerated implementation and iteration.

title: A workout, logged

notes.story: Demonstrate the working product using prepared demo data. If unavailable, walk through approved screenshots. Avoid exposing personal workout data accidentally.

title: An impressive result is a beginning

notes.point: An impressive result is a beginning
notes.story: Explain why generating code is different from delivering software. Review and judgment catch incorrect assumptions, bugs and inappropriate abstractions.

title: How I build with AI
body:
Problem → Experience → Requirements → Tasks
Agents → Review / test / debug → Feedback ↻

notes.story: Walk through the iterative process. Clear architecture, version control, automated tests and incremental changes make AI leverage dependable. Validate outcomes against real needs.

title: What would fit your work better?
body:
Administration · Spreadsheets · Internal tools
Business data · Services · Prototypes

notes.point: What would fit your work better?
notes.story: Invite recognition of repetitive work and poorly fitting tools. An existing product, simpler workflow or lightweight automation may be preferable to custom software.
notes.transition: Next: What would the ideal solution look like?

title: What would the ideal solution look like?
body:
Who needs it?
What gets in their way?
What would better look like?

notes.point: What would the ideal solution look like?
notes.story: Give the audience a moment to consider one problem. Investigate practicality after articulating the ideal outcome.
notes.transition: Next: What would be worth building?

title: What would be worth building?
body:
Think beyond your constraints.
Build with AI.
Deliver with discipline.

notes.story: Don’t start by asking what you can build. Start by asking what would be worth building. I help people turn ideas and problems into working software, combining product thinking, engineering experience, and AI-assisted development to make the process faster, more accessible, and more reliable. Invite conversation afterward.
